title: Observability data-plane segmentation + retention playbook
content:
Purpose
-----
This is a working playbook for how we should segment the observability data plane inside private deployments (VPCs and on-prem clusters), enforce retention tiers, and expose a minimal, secure upgrade path for our Terraform modules. The goal is to define pragmatic defaults that customers can adopt quickly while preserving a clear migration path to longer retention and archival.

Audience
--------
- Platform engineers implementing Private deployments
- SREs running on-prem clusters for customers
- Solutions engineering teams preparing customer proposals

Constraints we must respect
---------------------------
- No unrestricted internet egress by default in most private deployments.
- Customers may require data residency (on-prem or region-specific S3).
- Limited disk/IO on smaller bare-metal nodes — retention targets must be realistic.
- Encryption-in-transit and at-rest mandatory (TLS + KMS/HSM).
- Some customers will want zero external dependencies (air-gapped).

High-level design summary (recommended)
------------------------------------
1) Logical segmentation of telemetry flows:
   - Metrics (Prometheus remote_write) -> short-term TSDB (local Prometheus / Cortex/RW) for 15d hot retention -> long-term remote_write to object-store-backed ingester (Thanos/Cortex/Prometheus compatible) for 365d+ archival.
   - Logs (Fluent Bit / Fluentd) -> local buffer + tiered sink: nearline S3-compatible bucket (30d hot) -> cold vault (S3 Glacier or on-prem tape emulation) for >90d.
   - Traces/OTLP -> collector(s) with sampled forwarding to backend (Tempo/Jaeger compatible or third-party) and optional local span-store for 7d.

2) Control plane vs data plane:
   - Control plane (our management APIs, rollouts) stays in the customer VPC but uses mTLS to talk to customer-managed data-plane endpoints.
   - Data-plane components (collectors, forwarders, short-term storage) run in customer infra; where customers allow, we can run managed ingesters that accept secure, authenticated remote_write/OTLP over private networking.

3) Minimal allowed egress pattern:
   - VPC endpoint to object storage (S3 compatible) with IAM role-based write-only creds for telemetry buckets.
   - Optional direct-to-managed-ingester over private link with per-customer mTLS certs.

Terraform module interface (module: telemetry-data-plane) 
------------------------------------------------------
Notes: the module should be small and composable; it should not bake in a particular backend. Below are the variables we should expose (this is a draft of the README text, not TF code):

Variables (user-facing):
- telemetry_enabled (bool) - default true
- metrics_backend (string) - one of [local, cortex_remote_write, thanos_sidecar]
- metrics_retention_days (number) - default 15 (hot), note: long term archival handled by remote_write backend
- logs_backend (string) - one of [s3, loki, syslog]
- logs_hot_tier_days (number) - default 30
- s3_endpoint (string) - e.g., https://s3.company.internal or aws endpoint
- s3_bucket_name (string) - telemetry bucket
- encryption_kms_key_id (string) - optional; if empty use customer-managed key fallback
- otel_collector_config (string) - base64 encoded OTEL config override for advanced users
- enable_federation (bool) - allow federation scraping endpoints for central Prometheus
- prometheus_service_account (string) - SA used for scraping/remote_write
- egress_whitelist (list) - CIDR or endpoint list allowed for telemetry egress (string list)

Outputs (module should expose):
- prometheus_remote_write_url (string)
- otel_collector_endpoint (string)
- s3_telemetry_bucket (string)
- telemetry_kms_policy_arn (string)

Recommended defaults rationale
----------------------------
- Short hot retention (10-30 days) on local Prometheus cuts disk pressure and makes scraping predictable.
- Offload long-term retention to object-store backed systems (Thanos/Cortex) that scale horizontally or to customer S3 for compliance.
- Use per-customer mTLS certs for any direct-to-managed ingesters; do not allow plaintext endpoints.

Log shipping patterns (practical advice)
-------------------------------------
- Buffering: Fluent Bit must be configured with filesystem buffering for on-prem nodes (buffer_chunk_size small, buffer_max_size tuned to node memory).
- Backpressure: backpressure to local application should be a last resort; prefer persistent buffer + slow retries.
- Tagging: enrich logs with cluster_id, namespace, node_role, instance_id — keep schema stable for 6 months.

Prometheus + Federation vs remote_write tradeoffs
------------------------------------------------
- Federation (pull across clusters): simpler for ad-hoc query but increases cross-cluster network complexity and scraping load. Best for central ops that need live dashboards only.
- remote_write: preferred for long-term storage and for customers where cross-VPC scraping is disallowed. It provides batching and fewer open connections.

Upgrade plan (v1 -> v2 collectors / TF module change)
----------------------------------------------------
Phase 0: Preflight checks (run in parallel)
- inventory: list all clusters, collector versions, expected retention settings (scriptable via analytics query). (JIRA TF-301)
- run local dry-run of new TF module with --plan-only in staging org.
- ensure customers have IAM policy that can be updated for KMS if retention tier changes.

Phase 1: Canary customers (1-3 customers)
- Enable module in canary mode: still write to legacy backend plus new backend (dual-write).
- Monitor ingestion rates, disk pressure, error rates for 48–72 hours.

Phase 2: Broader rollout by cohorts (size-based)
- Small clusters -> medium -> large.
- Add automation to backfill short-term gaps via remote_read/export when switching TSDBs.

Phase 3: Cutover and cleanup
- After 7d stable, flip read traffic and remove legacy components.
- Run data-verification checks (sample metrics and histograms equality within tolerance).

Rollback strategy
-----------------
- Keep legacy remote_write endpoint available for 7 days after cutover.
- TF change rollbacks should be idempotent; module should provide an explicit "revert" flag that restores previous bucket/endpoint configs.

Smoke tests after upgrade (manual + automated)
---------------------------------------------
- Prom scrape success rate > 99% for 15 minutes post-deploy.
- Remote_write send success > 99% and no sustained 4xx/5xx spikes.
- OTEL: simple trace generated and visible in backend within 30s.
- Logs: tail a pod log and assert delivery to hot bucket within 60s.

Runbook snippets (copy-paste friendly)
------------------------------------
- To check collector health: kubectl -n telemetry get pods -l app=otel-collector -o wide
- Tail fluent-bit buffer size: kubectl exec -n logging fluent-bit-0 -- cat /buffers/status
- Verify remote_write: curl -k -u prometheus:token "${prometheus_remote_write_url}/healthz"

Cost/Capacity guidance (rough heuristics)
----------------------------------------
- Small cluster (5–10 nodes): plan for 2–4TB/day of log ingress -> use 30d hot tier (~60–120TB storage)
- Medium (20–50 nodes): 10–40TB/day -> consider object-store with lifecycle rules to move to cold after 30d
- Prometheus cardinality: if metrics cardinality > 50M series, require Cortex/Thanos with sharding.

Edge cases & air-gapped installs
--------------------------------
- Provide an "archive appliance" (vm/appliance) that customers can deploy to receive batched uploads via scp/rclone for purely air-gapped environments.
- Local-only mode: collectors write to on-disk rollups that can be exported for offline analysis.

Security considerations
-----------------------
- Key rotation: document a safe KMS key-rotation path. TF module should support key aliasing so rotation is key-id swap safe.
- Least privilege: write-only IAM policy for telemetry service role; no list/delete privileges on buckets from collectors.
- Audit logging: enable S3 access logs to a separate bucket with restricted access.

Open questions / TODOs
---------------------
- Decide default long-term backend: Thanos vs Cortex vs managed service? (tradeoffs: operational overhead vs cost) — ACTION: decide by 2026-03-01.
- Should we provide a hardened OTEL collector container image with built-in forwarding and buffering? (Pros: consistent behavior, cons: maintenance cost)
- TF API: do we expose blackbox credentials for s3 or prefer IAM role only? Need legal + sales input for customer expectations.

Notes to self / rough checklist for next edits
--------------------------------------------
- Convert variables list into a Terraform variables.tf reference and add examples for AWS S3, MinIO, and on-prem Ceph RGW.
- Add migration script example to backfill Prometheus TSDB to long-term storage (thanos bucket upload steps).
- Collect cost numbers from Finance for 3 retention tiers and embed an example pricing table.

References and quick links
-------------------------
- Prometheus remote_write docs: https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/remote_write/
- OTEL collector examples: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/examples
- Thanos bucket docs: https://thanos.io/tip/components/store.md/

-----

This document is a draft — expect many edits. If you're reviewing, please add inline comments or add TODO items as separate bullets so I can triage.
